content.text: {"relation":"REFINED","consensus_summary":"Justification is broadly a favorable forensic verdict by which God acquits or sets sinners right through Christ and grace, commonly formulated in Protestant theology as declaring them righteous through imputed righteousness. The verb can also mean vindicate, demonstrate, or acknowledge as right.","book_summary":"To justify is to judge, declare, or demonstrate a person, claim, deed, or cause right against a charge. It does not contradict the broader cross-traditional consensus that justification concerns a favorable divine judgment or being set right with God.","rationale":"The central legal referent is preserved: charge, judgment, acquittal, and the contrast with condemnation.
